podcast.body: Released on October 28th, 2013, this album was profoundly influenced by the band's extensive experiences in Haiti, where they absorbed Rara music, and by their studies of the Brazilian movie "Black Orpheus" and essays by Danish philosopher Soren Kierkegaard. James Murphy of LCD Soundsystem co-produced the album alongside Marcus Draves, known for his work with Coldplay. Recording sessions were held in Louisiana and Jamaica, with the Jamaican sessions notably taking place in an abandoned castle built in 1979. The album's cover artwork features Rodin's famous sculpture of Orpheus and Eurydice, tying into its thematic undercurrents. "Reflector Arcade Fire's fourth album released on October 28th, 2013."

podcast.body: This album contains two hidden tracks, one in the pre-gap area and another after the final listed song. The pre-gap track, officially listed as Track 0, is a 10-minute untitled piece of music played backwards, believed to be outtakes or "stillborn songs" from the album sessions. A second, untitled hidden track appears after "Supersymmetry" fades out. "If you have a CD copy of Arcade Fire's Reflector, try the put it in a CD player and hit rewind trick. You'll hear something, but it doesn't really sound right."

podcast.body: This album was presented as a double 180g vinyl set with a beautiful full-silver cover, representing a significant advancement in the band's physical releases. Its production notably included electronic elements, with James Murphy of LCD Soundsystem serving as a co-producer, marking the beginning of the band's trajectory towards more electronic musical territories. "el reflector, ese doble, disco en 180 g con esa portada en full plateado tan bonita."
